content: # ============================================================================= # app.R — LISP online calculator (Shinylive) # ============================================================================= # Upload any CSV, then assign the variable roles in the sidebar (ID, location, # response, explanatory variables) — column names are free; common names # (ID/lon/lat/y) are pre-selected automatically. Everything runs in the # visitor's browser via webR; no data leaves their device. # Method: Hu, Song & Zhang (2024), IJGIS, doi:10.1080/13658816.2024.2437811 # Figure arrangements follow the paper's Fig. 4, Fig. 5 and Fig. 6(a). # ============================================================================= library(shiny) source("lisp-core.R") source("lisp-plots.R") MAX_POINTS <- 2000 EXAMPLE_CSV <- "lisp-example-simulated.csv" BOUNDARY_CSV <- "boundary-greaterH.csv" sym_note <- function() tags$div(class = "note symtable", tags$b("Meaning of the symbols in the tables and figures:"), tags$ul( tags$li(HTML("q — local power of determinant (PD) of one explanatory variable: the geographical-detector Q statistic computed inside the local window centred at each location (paper Eq. 4), with its noncentral-F significance test (Eqs. 5–6).")), tags$li(HTML("ω — local PD of an interaction: ω0 for all variables together (regression-tree zones, GOZH, Eq. 7); ω1, ω2, … for variable pairs (cross-classification of the two discretised members).")), tags$li(HTML("a — range of the exponential semivariogram of the response: the distance where the fitted curve (practically) reaches the sill c (paper Fig. 4).")), tags$li(HTML("κ = multiplier × a — the local extent (paper Eq. 3, default multiplier 2): every location's window holds all points within κ.")), tags$li(HTML("Significance maps use the paper's classes: p < 0.01, p < 0.05, not significant.")) )) # -- UI ----------------------------------------------------------------------- ui <- fluidPage( tags$head(tags$style(HTML(" body { max-width: 1150px; margin: auto; } h2 { margin-top: 18px; } .well { background: #f7f9fb; } .note { color: #555; font-size: 13px; } .symtable ul { margin-bottom: 4px; } .symtable li { margin-bottom: 2px; } .cite { color: #555; font-size: 15px; border-left: 3px solid #4E79A7; padding-left: 10px; margin: 8px 0 22px 0; } .citehead { color: #333; font-size: 15px; margin: 22px 0 4px 0; } .dlrow { margin: 4px 0 18px 0; } .dlrow .btn { margin-right: 6px; } .scrollx { overflow-x: auto; } .scrollx table { font-size: 11.5px; white-space: nowrap; } .varlab { font-weight: 600; margin: 10px 0 2px 0; } table.data { font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; } .lisp-hex-zoom { transition: transform 0.15s ease; } .lisp-hex-zoom:hover { transform: scale(1.12); } ")), # A plot rendered while the tab is in the background gets width 0 and shows # an error; nudge Shiny to re-measure when the tab becomes visible again. tags$script(HTML(" document.addEventListener('visibilitychange', function() { if (!document.hidden) { setTimeout(function() { window.dispatchEvent(new Event('resize')); }, 250); } }); ")), # Browsers bypass the service worker for navigations (HTML # spec: downloads have service-workers mode 'none'), so in Shinylive the # native download click reaches the static host and 404s. Fetch the file # through the service worker instead and hand it over as a blob. tags$script(HTML(" document.addEventListener('click', function(e) { var a = e.target && e.target.closest('a.shiny-download-link'); if (!a || !a.getAttribute('href')) return; e.preventDefault(); fetch(a.href).then(function(resp) { if (!resp.ok) throw new Error('HTTP ' + resp.status); var cd = resp.headers.get('content-disposition') || ''; var m = /filename\\*?=(?:UTF-8'')?\"?([^\";]+)\"?/i.exec(cd); var filename = m ? decodeURIComponent(m[1]) : (a.download || 'download'); return resp.blob().then(function(blob) { var url = URL.createObjectURL(blob); var tmp = document.createElement('a'); tmp.href = url; tmp.download = filename; document.body.appendChild(tmp); tmp.click(); tmp.remove(); setTimeout(function() { URL.revokeObjectURL(url); }, 4000); }); }).catch(function(err) { alert('Download failed: ' + err.message + '. Compute the results first, then try again.'); }); }, true); "))), div(style = "display:flex; align-items:center; gap:16px; margin:18px 0 10px 0;", a(href = "https://yongzesong.com/app/lisp/", class = "lisp-hex-zoom", style = "flex:0 0 auto; line-height:0;", title = "LISP calculator", HTML('')), h2("LISP calculator — local indicator of stratified power", style = "margin:0;")), p(class = "citehead", "To cite LISP (local indicator of stratified power) in publications, please use:"), div(class = "cite", "Hu, J., Song, Y., & Zhang, T. (2024). A local indicator of stratified power. ", em("International Journal of Geographical Information Science. "), a(href = "https://doi.org/10.1080/13658816.2024.2437811", target = "_blank", "doi:10.1080/13658816.2024.2437811")), p(class = "note", "All computation runs locally in your browser (WebAssembly R). ", "Your data is never uploaded to any server."), sidebarLayout( sidebarPanel(width = 4, h4("1 · Data"), fileInput("file", "Upload CSV", accept = c(".csv", "text/csv")), div(class = "note", "Columns: an optional ID, longitude, latitude (WGS84 degrees), the ", "response y, and one or more explanatory variables. Column names ", "are free — after loading, assign the variable roles below (common ", "names such as ", code("ID"), "/", code("lon"), "/", code("lat"), "/", code("y"), " are pre-selected automatically). Recommended size: ", "up to ~1,000 points (hard limit ", format(MAX_POINTS, big.mark = ","), " for the in-browser version)."), actionButton("example", "Load example data", class = "btn-sm"), downloadButton("dl_sample", "Sample CSV", class = "btn-sm"), div(class = "note", style = "margin-top: 4px;", HTML("The example is a fully simulated dataset: 500 points ", "inside the LISP paper's Greater Himalayas study-area boundary, with ", "a response y and 8 simulated covariates named after the paper's ", "variable roles (slope, elevation, lake_area, precipitation, ", "summer_temp, winter_temp, aspect, albedo). None of the values are ", "real observations; the boundary is drawn on the example maps for ", "a paper-style presentation.")), hr(), h4("2 · Settings — variables"), div(class = "varlab", "ID (optional)"), selectInput("var_id", NULL, choices = c("None" = "")), div(class = "varlab", "Location (lon, lat)"), fluidRow( column(6, selectInput("var_lon", NULL, choices = c("lon…" = ""))), column(6, selectInput("var_lat", NULL, choices = c("lat…" = ""))) ), div(class = "varlab", "Response variable (y)"), selectInput("var_y", NULL, choices = c("Select…" = "")), div(class = "varlab", "Explanatory variables (x)"), selectInput("var_x", NULL, choices = character(0), multiple = TRUE, selectize = TRUE), hr(), h4("3 · Settings — parameters"), fluidRow( column(6, numericInput("vario_bins", "Variogram bins", value = 12, min = 6, max = 25, step = 1)), column(6, selectInput("vario_cutoff", "Variogram cutoff", choices = c("1/3 of max distance" = "3", "1/4 of max distance" = "4", "1/5 of max distance" = "5"), selected = "4")) ), numericInput("multiplier", HTML("Local extent multiplier (κ = multiplier × a)"), value = 2, min = 1, max = 4, step = 0.5), fluidRow( column(6, numericInput("discnum", "Discretisation bins", value = 4, min = 3, max = 8, step = 1)), column(6, numericInput("n_pairs", "Interaction pairs", value = 3, min = 1, max = 6, step = 1)) ), numericInput("n_strata", "Strata for the global benchmark", value = 5, min = 2, max = 10, step = 1), div(class = "note", "Defaults follow the LISP paper and its published pipeline: ", "multiplier 2 (Eq. 3), quantile discretisation with 4 bins, global ", "benchmark with 5 strata. Interaction pairs are chosen automatically: ", "the variable with the highest mean local q anchors the pairs, ", "partnered with the next-ranked variables (the paper's slope ∩ … ", "structure)."), hr(), h4("4 · Compute"), actionButton("compute", "Compute LISP", class = "btn-primary"), div(class = "note", style = "margin-top: 6px;", "The example takes roughly half a minute to one minute in the ", "browser; the regression-tree interactions are the slowest step.") ), mainPanel(width = 8, h4("Data preview — first 6 rows"), uiOutput("preview_ui"), h4("Data summary"), verbatimTextOutput("summary", placeholder = TRUE), h4("Local extent from the response semivariogram (paper Fig. 4)"), sym_note(), conditionalPanel("input.compute > 0", plotOutput("fig4", height = "430px")), div(class = "dlrow", downloadButton("dl_fig4_png", "Variogram PNG"), downloadButton("dl_fig4_pdf", "Variogram PDF (vector)")), uiOutput("fig4_info"), div(class = "scrollx", tableOutput("fig4_data")), div(class = "dlrow", downloadButton("dl_fig4_csv", "Variogram data CSV")), h4("Local power of individual determinants (paper Fig. 5)"), div(class = "note", HTML("For each explanatory variable: the local ", "q map (quintile classes over all variables), its significance ", "map, and the violin plot of the local power values (red dot = mean).")), uiOutput("fig5_ui"), div(class = "dlrow", downloadButton("dl_fig5_png", "Local q PNG"), downloadButton("dl_fig5_pdf", "Local q PDF (vector)")), div(class = "note", "First 10 locations; the full table is in the CSV."), div(class = "scrollx", tableOutput("fig5_data")), div(class = "dlrow", downloadButton("dl_fig5_csv", "Local q data CSV")), h4("Local power of interaction determinants (paper Fig. 6a)"), div(class = "note", HTML("ω0: interaction of all ", "variables (regression-tree zones); ω1, ", "ω2, …: the automatically chosen variable pairs, ", "each with its significance map; violin plot of the local power ", "values on the right.")), uiOutput("fig6_ui"), div(class = "dlrow", downloadButton("dl_fig6_png", "Interaction PNG"), downloadButton("dl_fig6_pdf", "Interaction PDF (vector)")), div(class = "note", "First 10 locations; the full table is in the CSV."), div(class = "scrollx", tableOutput("fig6_data")), div(class = "dlrow", downloadButton("dl_fig6_csv", "Interaction data CSV")), h4("Local vs. global power of determinants (paper Table 2)"), div(class = "note", HTML("Local PD statistics from LISP against the ", "global PD of the stratified-heterogeneity benchmark (quantile ", "strata for variables and pairs; regression-tree zones, GOZH, for ", "all variables). Significant locations use p < 0.05.")), div(class = "scrollx", tableOutput("table2")), div(class = "dlrow", downloadButton("dl_table2", "Comparison table CSV")) ) ), tags$details(style = "margin: 16px 0;", tags$summary("Method notes & data format"), tags$ul( tags$li(HTML("Local extent: empirical semivariogram of y (Eq. 1) on ", "great-circle WGS-84 distances, exponential model (Eq. 2) fitted ", "with gstat's np/h² weights; the range a is the effective ", "range (3 × the exponential parameter — where the curve ", "reaches the sill, as marked in the paper's Fig. 4), and ", "κ = multiplier × a (Eq. 3). Every location's window ", "holds the points within κ; windows with fewer than 10 ", "points fall back to the 10 nearest.")), tags$li(HTML("Local q of one variable (Eq. 4): quantile discretisation ", "inside the window, then the geographical-detector Q statistic ", "with the noncentral-F test (Eqs. 5–6), ported verbatim from the ", "GD package (Song et al. 2020). Undefined values follow the ", "published pipeline's convention: q → 0, p → 1.")), tags$li(HTML("Local ω of a pair: Q of the cross-classification of ", "the two discretised members. Local ω0 of all ", "variables (Eq. 7): zones from a regression tree (rpart, anova) ", "fitted inside the window — the GOZH approach (Luo et al. 2022).")), tags$li(HTML("Global benchmark (paper Table 2): the same Q statistic on ", "the full dataset — quantile strata for single variables and ", "pairs (OPGD-style), regression-tree zones for all variables ", "(GOZH-style).")), tags$li("Rows with missing values in any selected column are dropped ", "and reported."), tags$li("Implementation is verified against the GD, gdverse, localsp, ", "gstat and automap packages (agreement to machine precision ", "for q and its significance; see the project's validation ", "report). This tool computes LISP only — no geocomplexity ", "module.") )) ) # -- Server ------------------------------------------------------------------- server <- function(input, output, session) { raw <- reactiveVal(NULL) # list(df, label, is_example) boundary <- tryCatch(utils::read.csv(BOUNDARY_CSV), error = function(e) NULL) numericish <- function(v) is.numeric(v) || !all(is.na(suppressWarnings(as.numeric(v)))) # Load a data frame, then pre-select variable roles from common column names. populate <- function(df, label, is_example = FALSE) { names(df) <- trimws(names(df)) raw(list(df = df, label = label, is_example = is_example)) cols <- names(df) numcols <- cols[vapply(df, numericish, logical(1))] guess1 <- function(pat, from = numcols) { m <- from[grepl(pat, from, ignore.case = TRUE)] if (length(m)) m[1] else "" } g_id <- guess1("^(id|uid)$", cols) g_lon <- guess1("^(lon|longitude|x)$") g_lat <- guess1("^(lat|latitude)$") g_y <- guess1("^y$") g_x <- setdiff(numcols, c(g_id, g_lon, g_lat, g_y)) updateSelectInput(session, "var_id", choices = c("None" = "", cols), selected = g_id) updateSelectInput(session, "var_lon", choices = c("lon…" = "", cols), selected = g_lon) updateSelectInput(session, "var_lat", choices = c("lat…" = "", cols), selected = g_lat) updateSelectInput(session, "var_y", choices = c("Select…" = "", cols), selected = g_y) updateSelectInput(session, "var_x", choices = cols, selected = g_x) } observeEvent(input$example, { populate(utils::read.csv(EXAMPLE_CSV, check.names = FALSE), "Simulated example (500 points, Greater Himalayas boundary)", is_example = TRUE) }) observeEvent(input$file, { df <- tryCatch(utils::read.csv(input$file$datapath, check.names = FALSE), error = function(e) NULL) if (is.null(df)) { showNotification("Could not read that file as CSV.", type = "error") } else { populate(df, input$file$name) } }) # Current variable selection, validated. selection <- reactive({ r <- raw() validate(need(!is.null(r), "Load the example data or upload a CSV first.")) lon <- input$var_lon; lat <- input$var_lat; yv <- input$var_y idv <- input$var_id xs <- setdiff(input$var_x, c(lon, lat, yv, idv)) validate( need(nzchar(lon), "Select the longitude column (Settings — variables)."), need(nzchar(lat), "Select the latitude column (Settings — variables)."), need(nzchar(yv), "Select the response variable (Settings — variables)."), need(length(xs) >= 1, "Select at least one explanatory variable (Settings — variables)."), need(length(unique(c(lon, lat, yv))) == 3, "Longitude, latitude and the response must be three different columns.") ) list(id = idv, lon = lon, lat = lat, y = yv, x = xs) }) # Working dataset built from the selection: numeric, complete rows only. built <- reactive({ r <- raw(); s <- selection() used <- c(s$lon, s$lat, s$y, s$x) df <- r$df[, c(if (nzchar(s$id)) s$id, used), drop = FALSE] bad <- used[!vapply(r$df[, used, drop = FALSE], numericish, logical(1))] validate(need(!length(bad), paste0( "Selected column(s) not numeric: ", paste(bad, collapse = ", ")))) for (cc in used) df[[cc]] <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(df[[cc]])) keep <- stats::complete.cases(df[, used]) df <- df[keep, , drop = FALSE] validate( need(nrow(df) >= 30, paste0("Only ", nrow(df), " complete rows — at ", "least 30 are needed for a meaningful LISP.")), need(nrow(df) <= MAX_POINTS, paste0(nrow(df), " rows exceeds the ", "current limit of ", MAX_POINTS, " points for the in-browser version.")), need(all(abs(df[[s$lon]]) <= 360) && all(abs(df[[s$lat]]) <= 90), "Location values outside valid degree ranges — are these projected coordinates? This tool expects WGS84 degrees.") ) list(df = df, sel = s, dropped = sum(!keep), label = r$label, is_example = isTRUE(r$is_example)) }) result <- eventReactive(input$compute, { b <- built(); df <- b$df; s <- b$sel y <- df[[s$y]] X <- as.matrix(df[, s$x, drop = FALSE]) withProgress(message = "Computing LISP…", value = 0, { setProgress(0.02, detail = "distance matrix") D <- dist_matrix_km(df[[s$lon]], df[[s$lat]]) setProgress(0.06, detail = "semivariogram") vg <- empirical_variogram(y, D, nbins = max(6, as.integer(input$vario_bins)), cutoff = max(D) / as.numeric(input$vario_cutoff)) validate(need(nrow(vg) >= 4, "Too few variogram bins with data — increase the cutoff or the number of bins.")) fit <- fit_variogram_exp(vg) validate(need(!is.null(fit), "The exponential variogram fit failed — the response may carry no spatial structure at these distances.")) kappa <- as.numeric(input$multiplier) * fit$range windows <- local_windows(D, kappa, min_n = 10) setProgress(0.10, detail = "local q of individual variables") fres <- lisp_factor(y, X, windows, discnum = as.integer(input$discnum), progress = function(fr) setProgress(0.10 + 0.25 * fr, detail = "local q of individual variables")) n_pairs <- min(as.integer(input$n_pairs), ncol(X) - 1) pres <- NULL; pairs <- NULL if (n_pairs >= 1) { setProgress(0.35, detail = "local q of variable pairs") pairs <- choose_pairs(fres$q, n_pairs) pres <- lisp_pairs(y, X, windows, pairs, discnum = as.integer(input$discnum), progress = function(fr) setProgress(0.35 + 0.20 * fr, detail = "local q of variable pairs")) } setProgress(0.55, detail = "local interaction of all variables (regression trees)") ores <- lisp_omega_all(y, X, windows, progress = function(fr) setProgress(0.55 + 0.40 * fr, detail = "local interaction of all variables (regression trees)")) setProgress(0.96, detail = "global benchmark") tab2 <- table2_summary(fres, pres, ores, y, X, pairs, n_strata = as.integer(input$n_strata)) setProgress(1) list(df = df, sel = s, vg = vg, fit = fit, kappa = kappa, factor = fres, pairs = pairs, pair_res = pres, omega = ores, tab2 = tab2, is_example = b$is_example, dropped = b$dropped, label = b$label, win_size = vapply(windows, length, 1L)) }) }) # -- Data preview and summary ---------------------------------------------- output$preview_ui <- renderUI({ if (is.null(raw())) { return(div(class = "note", "Load the example data or upload a CSV to ", "see its first rows and columns here.")) } div(class = "scrollx", tableOutput("preview")) }) output$preview <- renderTable({ r <- raw(); req(r) utils::head(r$df, 6) }, striped = TRUE, digits = 3, class = "data") output$summary <- renderText({ r <- raw() if (is.null(r)) return("No data loaded yet.") s <- tryCatch(selection(), error = function(e) NULL) if (is.null(s)) { return(sprintf("Source: %s\nRows: %d, columns: %d\nAssign the variable roles in [2 · Settings — variables].", r$label, nrow(r$df), ncol(r$df))) } base <- sprintf( "Source: %s\nLocation: (%s, %s) Response: %s\nExplanatory variables (%d): %s", r$label, s$lon, s$lat, s$y, length(s$x), paste(s$x, collapse = ", ")) res <- if (input$compute > 0) tryCatch(result(), error = function(e) NULL) else NULL if (is.null(res)) return(paste0(base, "\nSet the parameters and press [Compute LISP].")) sprintf("%s\nComputed: %d points (%d dropped), range a = %.1f km, kappa = %.1f km, window size %d–%d (median %.0f).", base, nrow(res$df), res$dropped, res$fit$range, res$kappa, min(res$win_size), max(res$win_size), stats::median(res$win_size)) }) fmt3 <- function(x) sprintf("%.3f", x) # -- Fig 4: variogram ------------------------------------------------------- fig4_plot_fun <- function(res) plot_variogram(res$vg, res$fit, res$kappa) output$fig4 <- renderPlot({ fig4_plot_fun(result()) }) output$fig4_info <- renderUI({ res <- result() div(class = "note", HTML(sprintf( "Exponential fit (np/h² weights): nugget c0 = %.4g, ", res$fit$c0), sprintf( "sill c = %.4g, range a = %.2f km (effective range of the fitted ", res$fit$sill, res$fit$range), sprintf( "model), local extent κ = %s × a = %.2f km.", input$multiplier, res$kappa))) }) output$fig4_data <- renderTable({ res <- result() data.frame(`Distance (km)` = sprintf("%.1f", res$vg$dist), Semivariance = sprintf("%.5g", res$vg$gamma), `Point pairs` = res$vg$np, check.names = FALSE) }, striped = TRUE, class = "data") # -- Fig 5: local q of individual variables --------------------------------- res_frame <- function(res) { map_frame(res$df[[res$sel$lon]], res$df[[res$sel$lat]], if (res$is_example) boundary else NULL) } fig5_draw <- function(res) { items <- build_factor_items(res$factor) bins <- make_bins(as.vector(res$factor$q)) draw_lisp_figure(items, res_frame(res), bins, expression(italic(q)), expression("Sig. of" ~ italic(q)), "Local power value") } fig5_rows <- function(res) ceiling(ncol(res$factor$q) / 2) output$fig5_ui <- renderUI({ if (input$compute == 0) return(div(class = "note", "Press [Compute LISP] to render the figures.")) res <- result() plotOutput("fig5", height = paste0(fig5_rows(res) * 140 + 20, "px")) }) output$fig5 <- renderPlot({ fig5_draw(result()) }) fig5_table <- function(res, all = FALSE) { d <- res$df; s <- res$sel q <- res$factor$q; p <- res$factor$sig colnames(q) <- paste0("q_", colnames(q)) colnames(p) <- paste0("sig_", colnames(p)) out <- data.frame(d[, c(if (nzchar(s$id)) s$id, s$lon, s$lat)], q, p, check.names = FALSE) if (all) out else utils::head(out, 10) } output$fig5_data <- renderTable({ fig5_table(result()) }, striped = TRUE, digits = 3, class = "data") # -- Fig 6a: local interaction power ---------------------------------------- fig6_draw <- function(res) { items <- build_interaction_items(res$omega, res$pair_res) # Paper Fig 6a: one shared quintile legend over pairs + all variables; # violin ordered pairs first, all-variable omega_0 last. bins <- make_bins(unlist(lapply(items, `[[`, "q"))) draw_lisp_figure(items, res_frame(res), bins, expression(omega), expression("Sig. of" ~ omega), "Local power value", violin_items = rev(items)) } fig6_rows <- function(res) ceiling((1 + length(res$pair_res$labels)) / 2) output$fig6_ui <- renderUI({ if (input$compute == 0) return(NULL) res <- result() plotOutput("fig6", height = paste0(fig6_rows(res) * 145 + 20, "px")) }) output$fig6 <- renderPlot({ fig6_draw(result()) }) fig6_table <- function(res, all = FALSE) { d <- res$df; s <- res$sel out <- data.frame(d[, c(if (nzchar(s$id)) s$id, s$lon, s$lat)], omega0_all = res$omega$q, sig_omega0 = res$omega$sig, check.names = FALSE) if (!is.null(res$pair_res)) { q <- res$pair_res$q; p <- res$pair_res$sig colnames(q) <- paste0("omega_", res$pair_res$labels) colnames(p) <- paste0("sig_", res$pair_res$labels) out <- cbind(out, q, p) } if (all) out else utils::head(out, 10) } output$fig6_data <- renderTable({ fig6_table(result()) }, striped = TRUE, digits = 3, class = "data") # -- Table 2 ---------------------------------------------------------------- table2_pretty <- function(tab2) { data.frame( Group = tab2$Group, Variable = tab2$Variable, `Local PD of LISP mean [min, max]` = sprintf("%.3f [%.3f, %.3f]", tab2$`Local PD mean`, tab2$`Local PD min`, tab2$`Local PD max`), `Significant locations (p < 0.05)` = sprintf("%.2f%%", tab2$`Significant locations (%)`), `Global PD` = fmt3(tab2$`Global PD`), check.names = FALSE) } output$table2 <- renderTable({ table2_pretty(result()$tab2) }, striped = TRUE, class = "data") # -- Downloads -------------------------------------------------------------- # res 196 = 96 dpi x (3000 px / ~1470 px browser width): the PNG then # reproduces the browser's proportions exactly, so the compact row spacing # carries over to the export. png_of <- function(draw, w, h) function(f) { grDevices::png(f, width = w, height = h, res = 196) draw(); grDevices::dev.off() } # Vector export; Greek letters are drawn as plotmath, so the portable pdf() # device renders them on any platform. pdf_of <- function(draw, w_in, h_in) function(f) { grDevices::pdf(f, width = w_in, height = h_in, useDingbats = FALSE) draw(); grDevices::dev.off() } output$dl_sample <- downloadHandler( filename = function() "lisp-sample.csv", content = function(f) file.copy(EXAMPLE_CSV, f, overwrite = TRUE)) output$dl_fig4_png <- downloadHandler( filename = function() "lisp-variogram.png", content = function(f) { r <- result(); png_of(function() fig4_plot_fun(r), 1800, 1150)(f) }) output$dl_fig4_pdf <- downloadHandler( filename = function() "lisp-variogram.pdf", content = function(f) { r <- result(); pdf_of(function() fig4_plot_fun(r), 8, 5.2)(f) }) output$dl_fig4_csv <- downloadHandler( filename = function() "lisp-variogram-data.csv", content = function(f) { r <- result() out <- data.frame(dist_km = r$vg$dist, semivariance = r$vg$gamma, n_pairs = r$vg$np, nugget_c0 = r$fit$c0, sill_c = r$fit$sill, range_a_km = r$fit$range, kappa_km = r$kappa) utils::write.csv(out, f, row.names = FALSE) }) output$dl_fig5_png <- downloadHandler( filename = function() "lisp-local-q-maps.png", content = function(f) { r <- result() png_of(function() fig5_draw(r), 3000, round(196 / 96 * (fig5_rows(r) * 140 + 20)))(f) }) output$dl_fig5_pdf <- downloadHandler( filename = function() "lisp-local-q-maps.pdf", content = function(f) { r <- result() pdf_of(function() fig5_draw(r), 14, (fig5_rows(r) * 140 + 20) / 96)(f) }) output$dl_fig5_csv <- downloadHandler( filename = function() "lisp-local-q-data.csv", content = function(f) utils::write.csv(fig5_table(result(), all = TRUE), f, row.names = FALSE)) output$dl_fig6_png <- downloadHandler( filename = function() "lisp-interaction-maps.png", content = function(f) { r <- result() png_of(function() fig6_draw(r), 3000, round(196 / 96 * (fig6_rows(r) * 145 + 20)))(f) }) output$dl_fig6_pdf <- downloadHandler( filename = function() "lisp-interaction-maps.pdf", content = function(f) { r <- result() pdf_of(function() fig6_draw(r), 14, (fig6_rows(r) * 145 + 20) / 96)(f) }) output$dl_fig6_csv <- downloadHandler( filename = function() "lisp-interaction-data.csv", content = function(f) utils::write.csv(fig6_table(result(), all = TRUE), f, row.names = FALSE)) output$dl_table2 <- downloadHandler( filename = function() "lisp-table2-comparison.csv", content = function(f) utils::write.csv(result()$tab2, f, row.names = FALSE)) } shinyApp(ui, server)

name: lisp-core.R
content:
# =============================================================================
# lisp-core.R — LISP computation core for the browser (base R + rpart only)
# =============================================================================
# Local Indicator of Stratified Power, Hu, Song & Zhang (2024), IJGIS,
# https://doi.org/10.1080/13658816.2024.2437811
#
# Pipeline (paper Section 2):
#   1. Response semivariogram -> exponential fit -> range a -> local extent
#      kappa = multiplier * a (default 2, Eq 3). Each location's window is all
#      points within kappa.
#   2. Local power of individual determinants: quantile-discretised factor
#      detector q (Eq 4) with the noncentral-F significance test (Eqs 5-6)
#      inside every window.
#   3. Local power of interactions: q of the combined strata of a variable
#      pair, and omega of all variables via regression-tree (rpart) zones
#      (GOZH, Eq 7), inside every window.
#   4. Global benchmarks (OPGD/GOZH-style) for the Table-2-style comparison.
#
# The q statistic and its significance test are ported verbatim from GD::gd
# (Song et al. 2020) — including its treatment of singleton strata — and are
# verified against GD/gdverse/gstat/automap in validation/validate.R.
# Base R replaces sf/gstat/automap/localsp so the WebAssembly payload stays
# small; rpart has a prebuilt wasm binary on repo.r-wasm.org.
# =============================================================================

# -- Distances ----------------------------------------------------------------

# Great-circle distances (km) from one point to a set of points.
# Andoyer-Lambert approximation on the WGS-84 ellipsoid — the same formula as
# spdep's C gcdist() (src/dnn.c), so distances match spdep exactly.
gcdist_km <- function(lon0, lat0, lon, lat) {
  rad <- pi / 180
  a  <- 6378.137            # WGS-84 equatorial radius, km
  f  <- 1 / 298.257223563   # WGS-84 flattening

  F <- (lat0 + lat) / 2 * rad
  G <- (lat0 - lat) / 2 * rad
  L <- (lon0 - lon) / 2 * rad

  sinG2 <- sin(G)^2; cosG2 <- cos(G)^2
  sinF2 <- sin(F)^2; cosF2 <- cos(F)^2
  sinL2 <- sin(L)^2; cosL2 <- cos(L)^2

  S <- sinG2 * cosL2 + cosF2 * sinL2
  C <- cosG2 * cosL2 + sinF2 * sinL2

  w <- atan(sqrt(S / C))
  R <- sqrt(S * C) / w

  D  <- 2 * w * a
  H1 <- (3 * R - 1) / (2 * C)
  H2 <- (3 * R + 1) / (2 * S)

  d <- D * (1 + f * H1 * sinF2 * cosG2 - f * H2 * cosF2 * sinG2)
  d[!is.finite(d)] <- 0     # coincident points: S = 0 makes w, R undefined
  d
}

# Full symmetric distance matrix (km).
dist_matrix_km <- function(lon, lat) {
  n <- length(lon)
  D <- matrix(0, n, n)
  for (i in seq_len(n)) D[i, ] <- gcdist_km(lon[i], lat[i], lon, lat)
  (D + t(D)) / 2            # symmetrise the tiny asymmetries of the formula
}

# -- Semivariogram + exponential fit (paper Eqs 1-3) --------------------------

#' Empirical semivariogram (Eq 1) with equal-width distance bins.
empirical_variogram <- function(y, D, nbins = 12, cutoff = max(D) / 4) {
  idx <- which(upper.tri(D) & D <= cutoff & D > 0, arr.ind = TRUE)
  dd  <- D[idx]
  gg  <- 0.5 * (y[idx[, 1]] - y[idx[, 2]])^2
  br  <- seq(0, cutoff, length.out = nbins + 1)
  bin <- cut(dd, br, include.lowest = TRUE)
  out <- data.frame(
    dist  = as.vector(tapply(dd, bin, mean)),
    gamma = as.vector(tapply(gg, bin, mean)),
    np    = as.vector(table(bin))
  )
  out[!is.na(out$gamma) & out$np > 0, ]
}

#' Exponential model fit (Eq 2): gamma(h) = c0 + c * (1 - exp(-h / a_par)).
#'
#' The model is linear in (c0, c) given a_par, so a_par is profiled on a log
#' grid and (c0, c) solved by weighted least squares in closed form — more
#' robust than nls inside webR. Weights np/h^2 are gstat's default fit
#' criterion (fit.method = 7), which automap uses too.
#'
#' The reported range is the effective range 3 * a_par — the distance where
#' the exponential model first (practically) reaches the sill, which is what
#' the paper's Fig 4 marks as a. The local extent is kappa = multiplier * a.
fit_variogram_exp <- function(vg) {
  wt <- vg$np / vg$dist^2
  best <- NULL
  for (a_par in exp(seq(log(max(vg$dist) / 500), log(max(vg$dist)),
                        length.out = 400))) {
    X  <- cbind(1, 1 - exp(-vg$dist / a_par))
    # tiny a_par makes both columns ~constant; lsfit then warns "collinear"
    # before the fit is discarded — keep the console quiet about it
    cf <- tryCatch(suppressWarnings(
                     stats::lsfit(X, vg$gamma, wt = wt,
                                  intercept = FALSE)$coefficients),
                   error = function(e) NULL)
    if (is.null(cf) || cf[2] <= 0) next
    if (cf[1] < 0) cf[1] <- 0
    rss <- sum(wt * (vg$gamma - X %*% cf)^2)
    if (is.null(best) || rss < best$rss)
      best <- list(c0 = unname(cf[1]), c = unname(cf[2]), a_par = a_par,
                   rss = rss)
  }
  if (is.null(best)) return(NULL)
  best$sill  <- best$c0 + best$c
  best$range <- 3 * best$a_par
  best
}

#' Model curve for plotting.
variogram_curve <- function(fit, dmax, n = 200) {
  h <- seq(0, dmax, length.out = n)
  data.frame(dist = h, gamma = fit$c0 + fit$c * (1 - exp(-h / fit$a_par)))
}

# -- Local windows ------------------------------------------------------------

#' Indices of the points within `threshold` km of every location; windows
#' smaller than min_n fall back to the min_n nearest points (LPI convention).
local_windows <- function(D, threshold, min_n = 10) {
  n <- nrow(D)
  lapply(seq_len(n), function(i) {
    idx <- which(D[i, ] <= threshold)
    if (length(idx) < min_n) idx <- order(D[i, ])[seq_len(min(min_n, n))]
    idx
  })
}

# -- q statistic + significance (ported verbatim from GD::gd) -----------------

#' Factor-detector q and noncentral-F p-value of strata `x` for response `y`.
#' Port of FunQ inside GD::gd (Song et al. 2020) including its quirks:
#' singleton strata are removed from y, while the F degrees of freedom keep
#' the pre-removal counts. Returns c(q, sig); NA when undefined.
gd_q <- function(y, x) {
  x  <- factor(x)
  nx <- nlevels(x)
  ny <- length(y)
  if (nx < 2 || ny <= nx) return(c(q = NA_real_, sig = NA_real_))
  count.x <- table(x)
  k <- match(names(count.x)[which(count.x == 1)], x)
  if (length(k) > 0) {
    y <- y[-k]
    x <- factor(x[-k], levels = levels(x)[-which(count.x == 1)])
    count.x <- table(x)
    if (nlevels(x) < 1 || length(y) < 2) return(c(q = NA_real_, sig = NA_real_))
  }
  rss <- function(y) (length(y) - 1) * stats::var(y)
  sst <- rss(y)
  if (!is.finite(sst) || sst <= 0) return(c(q = NA_real_, sig = NA_real_))
  qv <- 1 - sum(tapply(y, x, rss), na.rm = TRUE) / sst
  v1 <- nx - 1
  v2 <- ny - nx
  Fv <- (v2 * qv) / (v1 * (1 - qv))
  m0 <- tapply(y, x, mean)
  m1 <- sum(m0^2)
  m2 <- sum(m0 * sqrt(count.x))^2 / ny
  lambda <- (m1 - m2) / (stats::var(y) * (ny - 1) / ny)
  sig <- tryCatch(1 - stats::pf(Fv, df1 = v1, df2 = v2, ncp = lambda),
                  error = function(e) NA_real_)
  c(q = qv, sig = sig)
}

#' Quantile discretisation into (at most) n bins; NULL when fewer than two
#' distinct bins exist.
disc_quantile <- function(x, n) {
  br <- unique(stats::quantile(x, probs = seq(0, 1, length.out = n + 1),
                               na.rm = TRUE, names = FALSE))
  if (length(br) < 3) {                 # fewer than 2 bins
    if (length(unique(x)) < 2) return(NULL)
    br <- unique(c(min(x), stats::median(x), max(x)))
    if (length(br) < 3) return(NULL)
  }
  cut(x, breaks = br, include.lowest = TRUE, labels = FALSE)
}

# -- LISP step 2: local power of individual determinants ----------------------

#' Local q and significance of every variable at every location.
#' Follows the LPI pipeline's NA convention: q -> 0, p -> 1.
#' progress: optional function(frac) called with completion in [0, 1].
lisp_factor <- function(y, X, windows, discnum = 4, progress = NULL) {
  n <- length(windows); vars <- colnames(X)
  qm <- matrix(0,   n, length(vars), dimnames = list(NULL, vars))
  sm <- matrix(1.0, n, length(vars), dimnames = list(NULL, vars))
  for (i in seq_len(n)) {
    w  <- windows[[i]]
    yw <- y[w]
    for (v in vars) {
      b <- disc_quantile(X[w, v], discnum)
      if (is.null(b)) next
      r <- gd_q(yw, b)
      if (is.finite(r["q"]))   qm[i, v] <- r["q"]
      if (is.finite(r["sig"])) sm[i, v] <- r["sig"]
    }
    if (!is.null(progress) && i %% 25 == 0) progress(i / n)
  }
  list(q = qm, sig = sm)
}

# -- LISP step 3a: local power of a variable pair -----------------------------

#' Automatic pair choice mirroring the paper: the variable with the highest
#' mean local q anchors the pairs, partnered with the next `n_pairs` ranked
#' variables (the paper's slope ∩ {lake area, summer temperature,
#' precipitation} structure).
choose_pairs <- function(qm, n_pairs = 3) {
  rank_vars <- names(sort(colMeans(qm), decreasing = TRUE))
  anchor    <- rank_vars[1]
  partners  <- rank_vars[-1][seq_len(min(n_pairs, length(rank_vars) - 1))]
  cbind(anchor, partners)
}

#' Local q and significance of variable pairs: the pair's strata are the
#' cross-classification of the two quantile-discretised members.
lisp_pairs <- function(y, X, windows, pairs, discnum = 4, progress = NULL) {
  n <- length(windows)
  labs <- paste(pairs[, 1], pairs[, 2], sep = " ∩ ")
  qm <- matrix(0,   n, nrow(pairs), dimnames = list(NULL, labs))
  sm <- matrix(1.0, n, nrow(pairs), dimnames = list(NULL, labs))
  for (i in seq_len(n)) {
    w  <- windows[[i]]
    yw <- y[w]
    for (p in seq_len(nrow(pairs))) {
      b1 <- disc_quantile(X[w, pairs[p, 1]], discnum)
      b2 <- disc_quantile(X[w, pairs[p, 2]], discnum)
      if (is.null(b1) || is.null(b2)) next
      r <- gd_q(yw, paste(b1, b2, sep = "_"))
      if (is.finite(r["q"]))   qm[i, p] <- r["q"]
      if (is.finite(r["sig"])) sm[i, p] <- r["sig"]
    }
    if (!is.null(progress) && i %% 25 == 0) progress(i / n)
  }
  list(q = qm, sig = sm, labels = labs)
}

# -- LISP step 3b: local omega of all variables (GOZH zones) ------------------

#' Local omega (Eq 7): regression-tree zones of all explanatory variables
#' inside each window (rpart, anova), then the zone q — the LPI pipeline's
#' run_gozh() applied per window.
lisp_omega_all <- function(y, X, windows, progress = NULL) {
  n <- length(windows)
  qv <- numeric(n); sv <- rep(1.0, n)
  for (i in seq_len(n)) {
    w <- windows[[i]]
    d <- data.frame(y = y[w], X[w, , drop = FALSE])
    tree <- tryCatch(rpart::rpart(y ~ ., data = d, method = "anova"),
                     error = function(e) NULL)
    if (!is.null(tree)) {
      zones <- as.character(tree$where)
      if (length(unique(zones)) >= 2) {
        r <- gd_q(d$y, zones)
        if (is.finite(r["q"]))   qv[i] <- r["q"]
        if (is.finite(r["sig"])) sv[i] <- r["sig"]
      }
    }
    if (!is.null(progress) && i %% 25 == 0) progress(i / n)
  }
  list(q = qv, sig = sv)
}

# -- Step 4: global benchmarks (Table-2-style comparison) ---------------------

global_q_var <- function(y, x, n_strata = 5) {
  b <- disc_quantile(x, n_strata)
  if (is.null(b)) return(c(q = NA_real_, sig = NA_real_))
  gd_q(y, b)
}

global_q_pair <- function(y, x1, x2, n_strata = 5) {
  b1 <- disc_quantile(x1, n_strata)
  b2 <- disc_quantile(x2, n_strata)
  if (is.null(b1) || is.null(b2)) return(c(q = NA_real_, sig = NA_real_))
  gd_q(y, paste(b1, b2, sep = "_"))
}

global_q_all <- function(y, X) {
  d <- data.frame(y = y, X)
  tree <- tryCatch(rpart::rpart(y ~ ., data = d, method = "anova"),
                   error = function(e) NULL)
  if (is.null(tree)) return(c(q = NA_real_, sig = NA_real_))
  zones <- as.character(tree$where)
  if (length(unique(zones)) < 2) return(c(q = NA_real_, sig = NA_real_))
  gd_q(y, zones)
}

#' Assemble the Table-2-style comparison: local mean [min, max], share of
#' significant locations, and the global PD, for individual variables, the
#' chosen pairs, and the all-variable interaction.
table2_summary <- function(factor_res, pair_res, omega_res,
                           y, X, pairs, n_strata = 5, sig_level = 0.05) {
  row_of <- function(name, group, qv, sv, gq) {
    data.frame(
      Group    = group,
      Variable = name,
      `Local PD mean` = mean(qv),
      `Local PD min`  = min(qv),
      `Local PD max`  = max(qv),
      `Significant locations (%)` = 100 * mean(sv < sig_level),
      `Global PD`     = unname(gq["q"]),
      `Global PD p`   = unname(gq["sig"]),
      check.names = FALSE
    )
  }
  rows <- list()
  for (v in colnames(factor_res$q)) {
    rows[[length(rows) + 1]] <- row_of(
      v, "Individual variable", factor_res$q[, v], factor_res$sig[, v],
      global_q_var(y, X[, v], n_strata))
  }
  if (!is.null(pairs) && !is.null(pair_res)) for (p in seq_len(nrow(pairs))) {
    rows[[length(rows) + 1]] <- row_of(
      pair_res$labels[p], "Interaction (pair)",
      pair_res$q[, p], pair_res$sig[, p],
      global_q_pair(y, X[, pairs[p, 1]], X[, pairs[p, 2]], n_strata))
  }
  rows[[length(rows) + 1]] <- row_of(
    "All variables", "Interaction (all)", omega_res$q, omega_res$sig,
    global_q_all(y, X))
  out <- do.call(rbind, rows)
  ord <- order(factor(out$Group, levels = c("Individual variable",
                                            "Interaction (pair)",
                                            "Interaction (all)")),
               -out$`Local PD mean`)
  out[ord, ]
}

name: lisp-plots.R
content:
# =============================================================================
# lisp-plots.R — paper-style figure drawing (base graphics only)
# =============================================================================
# Figure arrangements follow the LISP paper: Fig. 4 (variogram with a and
# kappa marked), Fig. 5 (per-variable local-q map + significance map pairs,
# violin on the right, shared quintile legend below), Fig. 6a (the same for
# omega_0 = all variables and the variable pairs). Colours are the paper's:
# quintile maps #5D9AD3 #7FC8CA #B3B3B3 #FBB03B #F15A24, significance
# #39B54A #ABDDA4 #B3B3B3, boundary/violin purple #AA66CD.
# =============================================================================

PALETTE_Q  <- c("#5D9AD3", "#7FC8CA", "#B3B3B3", "#FBB03B", "#F15A24")
SIG_COLS   <- c("#39B54A", "#ABDDA4", "#B3B3B3")
SIG_LABELS <- c("<0.01", "<0.05", "Not sig")
BOUNDARY_COL <- "#AA66CD"
VIOLIN_COL   <- "#AA66CD"

# Quintile classes over a pooled set of values (the paper's shared legend).
make_bins <- function(pool) {
  br <- unique(stats::quantile(pool, probs = seq(0, 1, 0.2), names = FALSE))
  if (length(br) < 3) br <- unique(seq(min(pool), max(pool), length.out = 6))
  if (length(br) < 2) br <- c(br, br + 1e-9)
  labs <- character(length(br) - 1)
  f <- function(v) sub("^0\\.", ".", sprintf("%.3f", v))
  for (i in seq_len(length(br) - 1)) {
    labs[i] <- sprintf("%s%s,%s]", ifelse(i == 1, "[", "("),
                       f(br[i]), f(br[i + 1]))
  }
  list(breaks = br, labels = labs)
}

bin_class <- function(v, bins) {
  cl <- cut(v, breaks = bins$breaks, include.lowest = TRUE, labels = FALSE)
  cl[is.na(cl)] <- 1L
  cl
}

sig_class <- function(p) ifelse(p < 0.01, 1L, ifelse(p < 0.05, 2L, 3L))

# Shared frame for all map panels of a figure; boundary = data.frame(ring,
# lon, lat) or NULL.
map_frame <- function(lon, lat, boundary = NULL) {
  xr <- range(c(lon, boundary$lon)); yr <- range(c(lat, boundary$lat))
  list(lon = lon, lat = lat, b = boundary, xr = xr, yr = yr,
       asp = 1 / cospi(mean(lat) / 180))
}

draw_map_panel <- function(fr, cols_pt, title_expr, cex_pt = 0.5) {
  par(mar = c(0.2, 0.2, 0.2, 0.2))
  plot(NULL, xlim = fr$xr, ylim = fr$yr, asp = fr$asp,
       axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "")
  if (!is.null(fr$b)) {
    for (rg in unique(fr$b$ring)) {
      bb <- fr$b[fr$b$ring == rg, ]
      graphics::polygon(bb$lon, bb$lat, border = BOUNDARY_COL, col = NA,
                        lwd = 1)
    }
  }
  points(fr$lon, fr$lat, col = cols_pt, pch = 16, cex = cex_pt)
  # The fixed aspect ratio letterboxes the map inside its cell, so a margin
  # title would float far above it; draw the title in data coordinates just
  # above the mapped extent instead.
  text(mean(fr$xr), fr$yr[2] + 0.05 * diff(fr$yr), title_expr,
       adj = c(0.5, 0), cex = 1.2, xpd = NA)
}

draw_violin_panel <- function(vals, labels_expr, ylab) {
  # pty = "s": the violin is square, as in the paper's Figs 5 and 6 — the
  # leftover space below it (bottom-right of the whole figure) hosts the
  # legends.
  par(mar = c(4.2, 4.0, 1.4, 0.4), mgp = c(2.5, 0.8, 0), pty = "s",
      cex.lab = 1.25)
  m <- length(vals)
  ylim <- range(unlist(vals))
  ylim <- ylim + c(-0.04, 0.08) * max(diff(ylim), 0.05)
  plot(NULL, xlim = c(0.45, m + 0.55), ylim = ylim, axes = FALSE,
       xlab = "", ylab = ylab)
  set.seed(1)
  for (i in seq_len(m)) {
    v <- vals[[i]]
    if (length(unique(v)) > 2) {
      d <- stats::density(v, from = min(v), to = max(v))
      w <- d$y / max(d$y) * 0.34
      graphics::polygon(c(i - w, rev(i + w)), c(d$x, rev(d$x)),
                        border = VIOLIN_COL, col = NA, lwd = 1.1)
    }
    points(i + stats::runif(length(v), -0.10, 0.10), v,
           pch = 16, cex = 0.22, col = grDevices::rgb(0, 0, 0, 0.30))
    points(i, mean(v), pch = 16, col = "red", cex = 0.85)
  }
  axis(2, las = 1, cex.axis = 1.05)
  axis(1, at = seq_len(m), labels = FALSE)
  is_expr <- is.expression(labels_expr)
  text(x = seq_len(m), y = graphics::par("usr")[3] -
         0.045 * diff(graphics::par("usr")[3:4]),
       labels = labels_expr, srt = if (is_expr) 0 else 38,
       adj = if (is_expr) c(0.5, 1) else c(1, 1), xpd = NA, cex = 1.05)
  box()
}

# Legends in the bottom-right blank left by the square violin (the paper's
# arrangement). Laid out side by side (value classes | significance) so the
# block stays shallow enough for compact map rows. `top` leaves headroom for
# the violin's rotated axis labels when they overflow (xpd) into this cell.
draw_legend_block <- function(bins, value_title, sig_title, top = 0.95) {
  par(mar = c(0, 0, 0, 0), pty = "m")
  plot.new()
  l1 <- legend(x = 0.02, y = top, legend = bins$labels, pch = 16,
               col = PALETTE_Q[seq_along(bins$labels)], ncol = 2, bty = "n",
               cex = 1.15, title = value_title, title.adj = 0)
  legend(x = min(l1$rect$left + l1$rect$w + 0.01, 0.78), y = top,
         legend = SIG_LABELS, pch = 16, col = SIG_COLS, ncol = 1, bty = "n",
         cex = 1.15, title = sig_title, title.adj = 0)
}

# Generic paper-style figure: items = list(list(title=, q=, sig=, and either
# vlab= (character) or vlab_expr= (plotmath)), ...); maps in two (q, sig)
# column pairs on the left, square violin in the upper right, and the
# legends in the blank below it (the paper's Figs 5/6 arrangement).
# violin_items allows a different panel order in the violin (paper Fig 6a
# reverses it).
draw_lisp_figure <- function(items, fr, bins, value_title, sig_title,
                             violin_ylab, violin_items = items) {
  k <- length(items)
  r <- ceiling(k / 2)
  M <- matrix(0L, r, 5); pid <- 0L
  for (j in seq_len(k)) {
    row <- ceiling(j / 2); cp <- ((j - 1) %% 2) * 2 + 1
    M[row, cp]     <- (pid <- pid + 1L)
    M[row, cp + 1] <- (pid <- pid + 1L)
  }
  violin_id <- pid + 1L
  legend_id <- violin_id + 1L
  if (r >= 2) {
    v_rows <- ceiling(r / 2)             # violin: upper part of the column
    M[seq_len(v_rows), 5]        <- violin_id
    M[(v_rows + 1):r, 5]         <- legend_id
    graphics::layout(M, widths = c(1, 1, 1, 1, 1.45))
  } else {
    # single map row: give the right column its own legend row below
    M[1, 5] <- violin_id
    M <- rbind(M, c(0L, 0L, 0L, 0L, legend_id))
    graphics::layout(M, widths = c(1, 1, 1, 1, 1.45),
                     heights = c(1, 0.85))
  }
  for (it in items) {
    draw_map_panel(fr, PALETTE_Q[bin_class(it$q, bins)], it$title)
    draw_map_panel(fr, SIG_COLS[sig_class(it$sig)], "Sig.")
  }
  has_expr_labels <- !is.null(violin_items[[1]]$vlab_expr)
  draw_violin_panel(lapply(violin_items, `[[`, "q"),
                    if (has_expr_labels)
                      do.call(expression,
                              lapply(violin_items, `[[`, "vlab_expr"))
                    else vapply(violin_items,
                                function(it) as.character(it$vlab), ""),
                    violin_ylab)
  # rotated character labels hang below the violin cell; keep headroom then
  draw_legend_block(bins, value_title, sig_title,
                    top = if (has_expr_labels) 0.95 else 0.72)
  graphics::layout(1)
}

# Fig 4: empirical semivariogram, fitted exponential curve, sill line, and
# the a / kappa verticals, as in the paper. Square plot region (pty = "s").
plot_variogram <- function(vg, fit, kappa) {
  cv <- variogram_curve(fit, max(vg$dist))
  op <- par(mar = c(4, 4.4, 1, 1), mgp = c(2.6, 0.8, 0), pty = "s")
  on.exit(par(op))
  ylim <- c(0, max(c(vg$gamma, fit$sill)) * 1.08)
  xlim <- c(0, max(c(vg$dist, kappa)) * 1.05)
  plot(NULL, xlim = xlim, ylim = ylim,
       xlab = "Distance (km)", ylab = "Semivariance")
  lines(cv$dist, cv$gamma, lwd = 1.6)
  points(vg$dist, vg$gamma, pch = 16, cex = 1.1)
  abline(h = fit$sill, lty = 2)
  abline(v = fit$range, lty = 2, col = "grey55", lwd = 1.4)
  abline(v = kappa, lty = 2, lwd = 1.4)
  yt <- ylim[2] * 0.55
  text(fit$range, yt, "a", pos = 4, offset = 0.4, cex = 1.0)
  text(kappa, yt * 0.82,
       bquote(kappa == .(sprintf("%.2f km", kappa))), pos = 4,
       offset = 0.4, cex = 1.0)
  text(xlim[2] * 0.015, fit$sill + 0.035 * ylim[2],
       bquote(italic(c) == .(sprintf("%.4g", fit$sill))),
       adj = c(0, 0), cex = 0.95)
  box()
}

# Item builders shared by the app and the offline figure tests.
build_factor_items <- function(factor_res) {
  lapply(colnames(factor_res$q), function(v) {
    list(title = v, q = factor_res$q[, v], sig = factor_res$sig[, v],
         vlab = v)
  })
}

build_interaction_items <- function(omega_res, pair_res = NULL) {
  items <- list(list(
    title = bquote(omega[0] * ": Interaction by all variables"),
    q = omega_res$q, sig = omega_res$sig,
    vlab_expr = bquote(omega[0])))
  if (!is.null(pair_res)) {
    for (p in seq_along(pair_res$labels)) {
      items[[p + 1]] <- list(
        title = bquote(omega[.(p)] * ": " * .(pair_res$labels[p])),
        q = pair_res$q[, p], sig = pair_res$sig[, p],
        vlab_expr = bquote(omega[.(p)]))
    }
  }
  items
}
